thinHeadings.heading: Reading the letter from a player's surname

Typing surnames only to save seconds

thinHeadings.heading: Keeping fallback names ready for deep letters
thinHeadings.under: Keep go-to names ready for the deep letters, because the wheel favors letters with lots of players left.

thinHeadings.heading: Resolving the ambiguity message quickly

thinHeadings.heading: Skipping instead of freezing on a blank

thinHeadings.heading: Ball Knowledge IQ rules for weighting, ranks and the daily set
The fixed ramp of twelve questions
thinHeadings.under: The 12 questions follow a fixed ramp: 3 easy, 3 medium, then pairs at rising weights up to the two hardest at the end.

thinHeadings.heading: Why the hardest questions move your IQ most
thinHeadings.under: Your IQ runs from 55 to 160 and is weighted by question value, so the hard ones move it most.

thinHeadings.heading: The same twelve questions every day
thinHeadings.under: Everyone gets the same 12 questions each day, and progress saves for the day.

Budgeting your focus for the back half
thinHeadings.under: Budget your focus for the back half. The final questions swing your IQ more than the first six combined.

thinHeadings.heading: Eliminating wrong options by detail
thinHeadings.under: Wrong options come from the same category and era as the answer, so eliminate by detail, not by vibe.

thinHeadings.heading: Shaking off an early red answer
thinHeadings.under: A red early answer changes nothing about the questions ahead, so shake it off.

thinHeadings.heading: Ball Knowledge IQ FAQ: the highest score, weighting and daily play
What is the highest possible IQ?
thinHeadings.under: 160, which needs a perfect 12 for 12. An all-wrong day scores the floor of 55.

thinHeadings.heading: Why did missing an easy one barely move my score?
thinHeadings.under: Scoring is weighted by difficulty. Early questions carry small weights, the final pair the biggest, so the deep cuts decide the number.

thinHeadings.heading: Is it the same test for everyone?
thinHeadings.under: Yes, same 12 questions in the same order for everyone each day, which is exactly what makes the share squares worth arguing over.
